subtopics.title: Rejuvenation — A River Made Young Again

questions.question: A graded river is one whose:
options: Long profile is a smooth concave curve with erosion and deposition in balance
Channel is perfectly straight
Source lies at sea level
Discharge is the same all year

questions.question: A eustatic cause of rejuvenation is:
options: Uplift of the land by tectonic forces
A worldwide fall in sea level, as when ice sheets lock up ocean water
The collapse of a waterfall
Deforestation of the catchment

questions.question: Uplift of the land rejuvenates a river because it:
options: Increases the rainfall over the basin
Widens the floodplain
Steepens every gradient along the profile, raising velocity and energy so vertical erosion resumes
Softens the bedrock beneath the channel

questions.question: The knickpoint of a rejuvenated river:
options: Stays fixed at the river mouth
Moves steadily downstream to the sea
Forms only in the source region
Marks where the new steep profile meets the old gentle one, and migrates upstream

questions.question: A South African waterfall often used to picture a retreating knickpoint is:
options: Howick Falls, where the uMngeni steps off the old surface into its deepening gorge
Victoria Falls on the Zambezi
The Tugela's coastal sandbar
A dolerite dyke in the Karoo

questions.question: Paired river terraces are:
options: Deltas built at the river mouth
Levees deposited during floods
Sandbanks on the inside of meander bends
Remnants of the old floodplain stranded at matching heights on both sides of the newly cut channel

questions.question: The valley-in-a-valley form consists of:
options: Two rivers sharing one channel
A fresh steep-sided V incised into the floor of a broad old valley
A gorge blocked by a landslide
A dry valley beside a wet one

questions.question: Entrenched and ingrown meanders differ in that:
options: Entrenched meanders occur only in deserts
Ingrown meanders are always older
Entrenched meanders are symmetric from rapid vertical cutting; ingrown meanders are asymmetric because the loops kept shifting sideways as they sank
Entrenched meanders carry no water

subtopics.title: River Capture — The Theft of a River

questions.question: The weapon by which a strong river captures its neighbour's headwaters is:
options: Lateral erosion across the floodplain
Deposition of a delta
Evaporation from its surface
Headward erosion — extending its source backwards through the watershed

questions.question: At the moment of capture, the weak river's upper course diverts into the captor because:
options: Water takes the lower, steeper exit that the breach offers
The captor's water is warmer
Wind pushes the water across the divide
The victim's channel is blocked by ice

questions.question: The elbow of capture is:
options: The waterfall at the knickpoint
The sharp, unnatural near-right-angle bend where the captured water swings into the captor's valley
The dry valley through the ridge
The delta of the captor stream

questions.question: A misfit stream is:
options: A stream flowing uphill
A stream that changes direction seasonally
The beheaded lower course of the victim — a stream far too small for the broad valley it occupies
The captured upper course of the victim

subtopics.title: Significance for People and Reading the Map

questions.question: A wind gap is useful to people because it:
options: Stores groundwater for boreholes
Generates wind power reliably
Provides fertile soils for orchards
Offers a ready-made pass through high ground for roads and railways

questions.question: River terraces attract settlement because they are:
options: Flat, fertile and above flood level
Rich in minerals
Always beside harbours
Cooler than the valley floor

questions.question: A deep incised gorge is attractive for dam builders because:
options: The water there is cleaner
A narrow gorge needs only a short, cheap dam wall
Gorges never experience floods
The rock in gorges is always soft

questions.question: Reliable map evidence of river capture includes:
options: A delta, a levee and a floodplain
A radial drainage pattern on a dome
An elbow bend, a dry wind gap through the ridge, and a misfit stream in an oversized valley
Crowded contours along both banks of a straight river

subtopics.title: The Old River Wins the Lottery

questions.question: In the lottery picture, the river's finish line — the level it can never dig below — is:
options: The floodplain
The watershed
Base level, normally the sea
The knickpoint

questions.question: The two ways the gap between river and finish line can suddenly widen are:
options: The sea falls, or the land rises
The river freezes, or the river floods
Rainfall doubles, or rainfall halves
The channel narrows, or the channel widens

questions.question: The renewed downcutting of a rejuvenated river spreads:
options: From the source downstream to the mouth
From the mouth upstream, as the knickpoint crawls toward the source
Evenly along the whole profile at once
Only within the floodplain

subtopics.title: Four Clues the River Got Young

questions.question: The four clues that a river has been rejuvenated are:
options: Delta, estuary, lagoon, sandspit
Source, mouth, tributary, confluence
Levee, floodplain, oxbow, scar
Knickpoint waterfall, paired terraces, valley-in-a-valley, incised meanders

questions.question: Terraces come in matching left-right pairs because:
options: Both banks are made of the same rock
They are the two stranded edges of one old floodplain the river cut down through
Farmers level them deliberately
The wind erodes both sides equally

questions.question: The 'snake that sank' describes:
options: A river that dried up in its channel
A straightened flood-control canal
Incised meanders — looping curves cut vertically into rock, as in Oribi Gorge
An oxbow lake filling with reeds

questions.question: Upstream of a retreating knickpoint waterfall, the river:
options: Still flows on its old, gentle profile
Has already cut down to the new level
Flows backwards
Always dries up

subtopics.title: The Neighbour Who Stole the Pipe

questions.question: In the boundary-wall picture, the strong river's advantage may include:
options: A steeper gradient, softer rock or more rainfall on its side
A wider floodplain and older terraces
A larger delta at its mouth
Warmer water in summer

questions.question: The five exhibits at the capture crime scene are:
options: Source, mouth, bank, bed, load
Captor stream, captured stream, elbow of capture, misfit stream, wind gap
Knickpoint, terrace, gorge, scar, delta
Watershed, basin, catchment, channel, floodplain

questions.question: A near-right-angle elbow in a river's course is treated as a confession of capture because:
options: All rivers bend at right angles eventually
Elbows only form in deserts
It marks the site of an old dam
Rivers never naturally turn that sharply — the bend records the diversion into the captor's valley

questions.question: After the capture, the captor stream often:
options: Dries up completely
Reverses its direction of flow
Rejuvenates, because its enlarged discharge gives it new erosive energy
Abandons its own valley
